choices.text: Agree - the mean is always the typical value
Disagree - the outlier drags the mean away from the bulk, so report the median alongside it
Agree - outliers never affect the mean
Disagree - the mode is always the typical value

questions.feedback: That mean-only answer is the one to unlearn: The mean always describes the typical score. Reteach point: The mean follows the outlier, the median resists it: report both when an outlier is present.
questions.misconception: The mean always describes the typical score.
questions.prompt: In a data set with one very large outlier, a classmate reports only the mean and calls it the typical value. Which response is correct?

questions.feedback: Scene s3 fixes this: the mean follows the total, 99 / 9 = 11 - the mean moved even though eight of the nine scores never changed.
questions.prompt: The top score in the nine-score data set rises from 18 to 27, so the total rises from 90 to 99. What is the new mean?

questions.feedback: Scene s6: the interquartile range is upper quartile minus lower quartile, 33.3 - 16.7, about 16.7 - the spread of the middle half of the data.
questions.prompt: Reading an ogive for 24 values gives lower quartile about 16.7 and upper quartile about 33.3. What is the interquartile range?

questions.feedback: Scene s4: cumulative frequency piles the frequencies up: 2 + 6 + 8 = 16, the third entry of the cumulative column.
questions.prompt: In the grouped table the class 20-30 has frequency 8. What is the cumulative frequency up to and including this class, if the classes before it have frequencies 2 and 6?
